title: libre_devops test results, version 1
description: What a checks role leaves on each host, as a fact whose name ends in _test_results, for libre_devops.test_results_report to read. One suite per checks role.

schema.description: The format and its version. Optional, but set it, so a later version of the format can tell old results apart.

suite.description: A stable id for the suite, usually the checks role's name, such as mde_linux_checks.

name.description: The suite's name for people. Defaults to the id.

properties.description: Facts about what was tested on this host, shown with the suite: the product version, its configuration and so on. Keep values short.

checks.description: One entry per check, in the order to show them. Check ids are unique within the suite.

id.description: A stable id. Waivers, limits and comparisons with earlier reports select checks by it, so never reuse one for a different check.

name.description: What the check proves, as a statement that is true when it passes, such as "Real-time protection is enabled".

status.description: passed and failed: the check ran and the answer was yes or no. error: the check could not get an answer (a command failed or timed out). skipped: it did not apply; say why in detail.

severity.description: How much a failure matters. The report's fail_severity decides which severities count against the verdict.

category.description: A grouping such as installation, protection, stability or performance.

detail.description: One line saying what was found, for the report's tables. For a skipped check, why it was skipped.

remediation.description: What to do when it fails.

docs.description: A link to the documentation for the failure.

output.description: Evidence: command output, a log excerpt. The JSON report keeps 64 KiB of it, the Markdown report output_limit characters.

metrics.description: Numbers the check measured, for limits and comparisons. Put the unit in the name, Prometheus style: duration_seconds, memory_mib, cpu_percent.
